name: InputOTP
import: import { InputOTP, InputOTPGroup, InputOTPSlot, InputOTPSeparator } from '@theya/shadcn/ui/input-otp';
description:
Segmented one-time-code field on the headless `input-otp` library.
Renders one real <input>; put `aria-invalid` on <InputOTP> itself (not
a slot) since that's the single real focusable element the library
mounts. Pair with visible, described error text via aria-describedby
— the danger border alone isn't sufficient (color-only signal).
whenToUse: A one-time code of known length from an SMS, email or authenticator app.

whenNotToUse.text: Codes of varying length, or recovery codes with dashes
Anything that isn’t a code (PINs people set themselves)

anatomy.description: one real input under the slots; `maxLength`, `pattern`, `inputMode`.
one per character, grouped like the code is shown (3 + 3).

do.caption: One field under the hood: paste and autofill fill every slot.
do.example:
<InputOTP maxLength={6} inputMode="numeric" aria-label="Verification code">
  <InputOTPGroup>
    {[0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5].map((i) => (
      <InputOTPSlot key={i} index={i} />
    ))}
  </InputOTPGroup>
</InputOTP>

dont.caption: Separate fields break paste, autofill and Backspace.

a11y: Put `aria-invalid` on InputOTP itself and describe the error in text — the red border alone isn’t enough.
